  ### 4. Forensic evaluation layer (offline, cron/agent — never in a hook)    
                                                                              
  Joins ab-serves.jsonl to (a) ratings.jsonl (SatisfactionCapture, keyed by   
  session_id + ts) and (b) in-session recurrence derived from the serve log   
  itself.                                                                     
                                                                              
  • TOKEN COST = mean served_tokens (direct) + recurrence as downstream proxy.
  • EFFECTIVENESS (for a corrective guard) = 1 - recurrence_rate, where       
  recurrence =                                                                
  the SAME module re-firing later in the SAME session (== the nudge did NOT   
  change                                                                      
  behavior). This is the ground-truth-ish behavioral signal.                  
  • mean_next_rating from SatisfactionCapture is a SECONDARY, weaker signal.  
  • Composite: efficiency = effectiveness / mean_tokens. Challenger wins if   
  cheaper &                                                                   
  not behaviorally worse (two-proportion z-test, min n=30 guard), or          
  significantly                                                               
  more effective (z>1.96). Optional LLM-judge path over sampled post-serve    
  transcript                                                                  
  windows for a stronger label than the recurrence proxy.                     
                                                                              
  ### 5. Refactor shape — hooks/lib/ab-serve.ts shared helper                 
                                                                              
  Single one-line adoption per module:                                        
  reason = serveVariant({hook, module, session_id, turn_index,                
  fields:{labels, snippet}, fallback: buildXNudge(matches)}).message          
  The current buildXNudge() stays UNTOUCHED and becomes the fallback/control. 
  Fail-open + flag-gated (FLAGS.json abtest.enabled, default false): with the 
  flag                                                                        
  OFF, or no variant file, or any error, serveVariant returns the fallback    
  verbatim.                                                                   
  The load-bearing hooks are BYTE-IDENTICAL to today until a challenger is    
  added.                                                                      
                                                                              
  ## Prototype (verified, isolated — NOT wired into live hooks)               
                                                                              
  Location: scratchpad/abtest-proto/ (see report). Files: lib/ab-serve.ts,    
  variants/yolo-deferral.json (control 118tok / terse-v1 41tok / imperative-v1
  27tok),                                                                     
  fake-hook.ts (minimal-adoption BehaviorEnforcement stand-in), forensic-     
  eval.ts,                                                                    
  run-demo.ts + run-demo.sh (300-session simulation with a HIDDEN ground-truth
  winner).                                                                    
  Verified: flag-off returns fallback verbatim; session-stickiness holds;     
  weighted                                                                    
  spread ~1:1:1; forensic-eval RECOVERS the hidden winner (imperative-v1:     
  recurrence                                                                  
  0.219 vs control 0.483, z=4.71, 24 vs 144 tokens = ~9x efficiency).         
                                                                              
  ## The hard part (honest)                                                   
                                                                              
  Attributing a behavioral outcome to a phrasing variant is NOISY.            
  Mitigations:                                                                
                                                                              
  1. Session-stickiness so a session isn't split across variants.             
  2. Recurrence (guard re-fires) as the primary signal — it's a real behavior,
  not a                                                                       
  sentiment guess. SatisfactionCapture ratings are a KNOWN-degraded signal    
  right now                                                                   
  (its inference path is frequently timing out at 15s and defaulting to       
  rating=5 —                                                                  
  observed live), so the design leans on recurrence and treats ratings as     
  secondary.                                                                  
  3. Min-sample + z-test gating so low-volume modules don't produce false     
  winners.                                                                    
  4. Confounds remain: task difficulty, session length, model drift, and the  
  corrective                                                                  
  only fires when the anti-pattern already occurred (selection effect). The   
  framework                                                                   
  MEASURES lift, it does not prove causation — periodic control holdback +    
  optional                                                                    
  LLM-judge are the escalation path when a challenger looks like a winner.

## 2. Hostname and TLS

1. Name: `sidecar.trilliumsmith.com`. It matches the `<service>.trilliumsmith.com` pattern of the bridge plan (task-pt5ji: `bridge.trilliumsmith.com`).
2. DNS: `trilliumsmith.com` NS is Vercel (`ns1/ns2.vercel-dns.com`). A wildcard `*.trilliumsmith.com` resolves to Vercel (216.198.79.1/65, 64.29.17.1), so `sidecar.trilliumsmith.com` points at Vercel **today**. An explicit `A sidecar 198.12.123.41` record beats the wildcard. Create it **before** the Caddy reload, or the ACME HTTP/TLS-ALPN challenge lands on Vercel and fails (then retries with back
3. TLS: Caddy's automatic HTTPS issues a Let's Encrypt certificate (as for `vps01.trilliumsmith.com`). It needs no extra config. HSTS is set without `includeSubDomains`, so other `*.trilliumsmith.com` hosts are unaffected.
4. Leg two (vps01 → MacBook) is https to the tailnet twin. Caddy verifies the MacBook's `macbook.hippo-tilapia.ts.net` certificate with `tls_server_name`. tailscaled picks the serve handler by **SNI** (`ipn/ipnlocal/serve.go:824-835`, v1.104.1), so the SNI must be the ts.net name while the Host header stays public.

## 3. Auth in front, and why the upstream is the :8792 twin

### 3.1 Sidecar's gate is the auth
- `--require-auth` accepts an admin/device token, the `sidecar_access` cookie, or the QR `sidecar_pane` cookie, and nothing else.
- Cookies are `Secure` when `r.TLS != nil` **or** `X-Forwarded-Proto: https` (`internal/server/access.go:189`; branch `internal/server/pair.go:77`). tailscale serve sets `X-Forwarded-Proto: https` (`serve.go:1089-1094`), so cookies stay Secure through the chain.
- Basic auth was ruled out. It would break the cookie-less QR pairing page and PWA install, and the captain chose Sidecar's gate (task-k2354).

### 3.2 Through the twin, the public request is a loopback peer
- tailscale serve proxies to `127.0.0.1:8791`, so Sidecar's `r.RemoteAddr` is loopback.
- `tailnet.Peer` never treats loopback as tailnet (`internal/tailnet/tailnet.go:23-29`). So `Trust.Trusted` returns false at step 1 (`tailnet.go:104-107`), and `Approver.Judge` rejects (`internal/tailnet/approve.go:51-54`).
- The branch's `--pair-via-serve` path (`internal/tailnet/served.go`) accepts a loopback approval only when **all** of these hold:
  - Host equals the pair-origin host (`macbook.hippo-tilapia.ts.net:8792`);
  - there is no `Tailscale-Funnel-Request`;
  - there is exactly one `Tailscale-User-Login`;
  - whois agrees.
- A public request fails that on Host (the edge keeps `sidecar.trilliumsmith.com`). It also fails on identity: vps01 is `tag:vps`, and tailscaled sets **no** user identity for a tagged node and deletes every client-sent `Tailscale-User-*`/`-Funnel-Request`/`-Headers-Info` header (`serve.go:1100-1123`). The edge also strips them itself, as defence in depth.
- Host is preserved end to end (`serve.go:995`, `r.Out.Host = r.In.Host`). That keeps three things working:
  - the same-origin write check, which compares the `Origin` host with `r.Host` (`internal/server/access.go:203-214`);
  - the default-pane address shown to the user (`core.View(id, host)`);
  - the fallback approve URL.

### 3.3 Why not the direct listener `100.74.138.74:8791` (Option A)
- There, Sidecar sees vps01's own tailnet IP as the TCP peer. Tailnet trust then turns on `HostOK(r.Host)` alone (`tailnet.go:53-69, 108`).
- It is safe only while Caddy forwards the public Host. One `header_up Host macbook...` or `{upstream_hostport}` edit would hand internet visitors tokenless reads and, with an empty `--pair-approvers`, self-approval of their own QR claim.
- The twin removes that footgun. The snippet carries a comment saying never to rewrite Host.

### 3.4 Pre-existing exposure (present today, without any proxy)

| `curl http://100.74.138.74:8791/healthz` | 200 |

- Impact once vps01 is the internet edge: a vps01 compromise gives Sidecar reads, plus pane approval if `--pair-approvers` is empty.

# Install as /etc/caddy/sites/sidecar.trilliumsmith.com.caddy and pull it in from /etc/caddy/Caddyfile with ONE line:
#   import /etc/caddy/sites/sidecar.trilliumsmith.com.caddy
# Stock Caddy, no plugins. This file holds no secret.
#
# Upstream is the tailnet-only https twin (tailscale serve :8792 -> 127.0.0.1:8791 on the MacBook), NOT the direct
# tailnet listener 100.74.138.74:8791. Through the twin Sidecar sees a loopback TCP peer, which it never tailnet-trusts
# and never accepts as a pairing approver; tailscaled strips every client-sent Tailscale-* identity header and names
# no user for a tagged node (vps01 is tag:vps). The direct listener would judge the request on vps01's own tailnet
# address and be safe only while the Host header below stays the public name.
#
# Auth: Sidecar's own --require-auth gate (admin/device token, sidecar_access cookie, QR sidecar_pane cookie).
# No basic_auth in front: it would break the cookie-less QR pairing page and the PWA install surface.
sidecar.trilliumsmith.com {
	header {
		Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000"
		X-Robots-Tag "noindex, nofollow, noarchive"
		Referrer-Policy "no-referrer"
		X-Content-Type-Options "nosniff"
		-Server
	}

	request_body {
		max_size 1MB
	}

	# Approval and operator-only routes stay on the tailnet. A pane never needs them; an approval must come from
	# the tailnet twin (the QR's --pair-origin), never from the internet.
	@tailnet_only {
		path /pair /pair/* /v1/pane-claims/*/approve /v1/doctor /v1/audit /v1/notify /v1/commands /v1/show /v1/join-tokens /v1/join-tokens/*
	}
	handle @tailnet_only {
		respond "Not found" 404
	}
	@claims_list {
		method GET
		path /v1/pane-claims
	}
	handle @claims_list {
		respond "Not found" 404
	}
	@app_writes {
		method PUT DELETE
		path /v1/apps/*
	}
	handle @app_writes {
		respond "Not found" 404
	}

	handle {
		reverse_proxy https://100.74.138.74:8792 {
			# Keep the public name. NEVER rewrite Host to a tailnet name (macbook, *.ts.net, 100.x): Sidecar's
			# tailnet trust and approver accept those, and its same-origin check compares Origin with Host.
			header_up Host {host}
			header_up -Tailscale-User-Login
			header_up -Tailscale-User-Name
			header_up -Tailscale-User-Profile-Pic
			header_up -Tailscale-Funnel-Request
			header_up -Tailscale-Headers-Info
			header_up -Tailscale-App-Capabilities

Check the **LAST SEEN** and **UPDATED** columns. Current result:

1. Run `SIDECAR_URL=http://macbook:8791 sidecar devices` and `... sidecar panes`.
2. Treat a pane as stale if its device is offline and the pane's `UPDATED` is old.

Right now:
- **Stale:** `dev-ff3c49` (MacIntel browser) is offline, last seen 5h ago. Its pane `dev-ff3c49` shows the `decisions` app, last updated 8h ago. Nothing on that screen is current.
- **Live:** `dev-b468a9` (Linux browser) is online, seen 2s ago. Its pane updated 54s ago.

How the server decides, from the source:
- A device is online if it was seen within its lease window (`internal/registry/registry.go:74`).
- `sidecar doctor` flags a pane as stale when its device has been offline more than 10 minutes (`internal/doctor/fleet.go:11`, `:50`).
- The `decisions` app on a stale pane can't be acted on until that device comes back online. Reopen the shell on that device to refresh it.

`doctor` needs the admin token, and I didn't read it. To run it, pass `--token-file` yourself, or use the browser sign-in at `/?token=…`.

**Note:** the paired phone or device name `dev-ff3c49` is the MacBook browser that was online earlier; no action is needed unless you want that screen current.

sidecar - drive the display panes of a running 'sidecar serve'

Usage: sidecar <command> [subcommand] [flags]

Server:
  serve        run the HTTP API and browser shell (see 'sidecar serve -h')

Commands:
  devices      enrolled displays
  uis          available UIs: what each display can do and be driven to
  panes        UI slots on devices
  apps         whitelisted apps a pane may be driven to
  drive        switch a pane to a whitelisted app, or back to default
  show         put a file, dev-server page or directory on the captain's pane
  notify       send a push notification to subscribed phones (Web Push)
  fullscreen   maximize a pane (hide the chrome, fill the display), or restore it
  watch        tail a pane's event stream (SSE) with cursor replay
  affordances  list what a device's screen offers to operate
  invoke       operate a declared action on a device's screen
  requests     questions asked of the user, with answers routed back
  status       server health, config, and counts at a glance
  doctor       check the server: state, token, listen/auth/TLS, app URLs, devices, panes, tailnet names (`doctor names` probes every service by short name and FQDN)
  audit        screen-use audit: how much of a pane, app or page is content, blank, clipped or chrome
  completion   print a shell completion script (bash, zsh, fish)
  help         show help for a command

Global flags (any command, any position):
  --url URL          server base URL        (env SIDECAR_URL, default http://localhost:8787)
  --token T          bearer token           (env SIDECAR_TOKEN)
  --token-file FILE  file holding the token (env SIDECAR_TOKEN_FILE)
  --json             machine-readable output; errors go to stderr as JSON
  --timeout D        HTTP timeout per call  (default 15s)

Reads need no token; writes (drive, apps add/rm, requests ask/cancel/redeliver)
need the admin token. Bare groups run their list command: 'sidecar panes'.

Exit codes:
  0 ok   1 error   2 usage   3 not found   4 auth   5 conflict/loop
  6 rejected (validation, app not allowed, capability mismatch)
  7 rate limited   8 server unreachable   9 no answer (wait timed out, cancelled, expired)
  10 unhealthy (doctor / devices diag found a failing check)

Examples:
  sidecar uis list --touch
  sidecar drive left clock

# QR pairing: a pane that is not on the tailnet

A pane that cannot be authenticated by where it comes from — loopback, a LAN tablet, or the `tailscale serve`
https twin, which arrives from `127.0.0.1` — shows a code. A device on the tailnet scans it and approves the pane.
The pane then has an ordinary Sidecar session.

It exists to delete one piece of friction and one residual risk:

- `README.md` "Install on a phone": the https install address still needs `?token=`, because `tailscale serve`
  arrives from loopback and tailnet trust refuses loopback by design.
- `docs/security-review.md` "The sign-in URL carries the admin token": `?token=<admin>` pastes the admin token into
  a URL that can stay in browser history or sync to other devices.

Off by default. Turn it on with `serve --pane-pair --require-auth`.

---

## 1. The flow

```
  P (pane, no credential)                       A (phone, on the tailnet)
  ───────────────────────                       ────────────────────────
1 GET /  (Accept: text/html)
  → the pairing page, not a JSON 401
      ↳ POST /v1/pane-claims
        → 201 {claim{id,code,phrase}, nonce, approve_url, qr}
        Set-Cookie: sidecar_claim=<id>.<hmac>   (HttpOnly)
      ↳ paints the QR on a canvas from `qr`
                                   2 scan → GET /pair/<CODE>
                                        → the confirm page: the pane's address,
                                          its browser, and the same phrase
3                                                POST /v1/pane-claims/<CODE>/approve
                                                   {label?}
                                                 ← 200 {claim{state:"approved",
                                                          approved_by{node,stable_id}}}
      ↳ polls GET /v1/pane-claims/<id> every 2 s
        → state:"approved"
        ↳ POST /v1/pane-claims/<id>/claim {nonce, capabilities, viewport}
          → 201 {device, pane, token:"dt_…", config, view}
          Set-Cookie: sidecar_pane=<dev>.<hmac> (HttpOnly)
        ↳ stores {id, token} under the shell's own localStorage key, reloads /
      ↳ GET / passes on sidecar_pane → the ordinary shell
```

Neither the code nor the QR is a credential. Approving a code does not hand out a session: the session goes to
whoever presents the `sidecar_claim` cookie **and** the nonce the pane holds in script memory, once.

Sidecar lifecycle

1. Device and pane lifecycle (state)

flowchart TD
  start([sidecar serve starts]) --> unknown[Pane shows nothing yet]
  unknown -->|no credential, pairing on| pairing[Pairing page shows a code and QR]
  unknown -->|admin or open enroll| enroll[POST /v1/devices]
  pairing -->|tailnet phone approves| claim[Pane claims a device token]
  claim --> enroll
  enroll --> online[Device online: heartbeat and viewport]
  online -->|heartbeat within lease| online
  online -->|no heartbeat past lease| offline[Device offline, last seen shown]
  offline -->|shell reconnects| online
  online --> default[Pane in default mode: self-describing]
  default -->|drive to whitelisted app| app[Pane shows an app]
  app -->|drive default or show --back| default
  online -->|PATCH scale 1.0 to 2.5| online
  online -->|fullscreen on or off| online
  offline -->|DELETE device| gone([Device removed])
  classDef bad fill:#fde2e2,stroke:#c33
  class offline bad

2. Pairing a pane with no credential (sequence)

sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  participant P as Pane without credential
  participant S as Sidecar server
  participant A as Approver phone on tailnet
  P->>S: GET / (asks for HTML)
  S-->>P: Pairing page
  P->>S: POST /v1/pane-claims
  S-->>P: claim id, code, phrase, QR (cookie sidecar_claim)
  P->>P: Paint QR
  A->>S: Scan QR, GET /pair/CODE
  S-->>A: Confirm page: pane address, browser, phrase
  A->>S: POST /v1/pane-claims/CODE/approve
  S-->>A: approved
  loop every 2 seconds
    P->>S: GET /v1/pane-claims/id
  end
  S-->>P: state approved
  P->>S: POST /v1/pane-claims/id/claim (nonce, capabilities, viewport)
  S-->>P: device, pane, token dt_ (cookie sidecar_pane)
  P->>P: Store token, reload into the shell

3. Driving a screen and asking a question (sequence)

sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  participant C as Captain or agent with admin token
  participant S as Sidecar server
  participant V as Pane shell in browser or phone
  C->>S: POST /v1/commands drive pane to app
  S-->>V: SSE event on /v1/panes/id/events
  V->>V: Render whitelisted app
  C->>S: POST /v1/requests ask the user
  S-->>V: SSE event with pending question
  V->>C: Question shown on the pane
  V->>S: POST /v1/requests/id/reply
  S-->>C: Answer routed back to the asker (GET request with wait)
  C->>S: POST /v1/commands drive pane to default
  S-->>V: SSE event, pane returns to default

Notes

Drawn from Sidecar's own docs: pairing.md section 1, api.md sections 4 to 6, and the lease check in internal/registry/registry.go. Labels are paraphrased, not exact route names beyond those cited.

# Sidecar through the vps01 reverse proxy: exposure plan (task-k2354)

Plan only. Nothing was enabled. No vps01 file was edited (re-checked by task-us7sh: still none). No Funnel was touched. This report holds no secret.

## 0. Verdict (updated 2026-10-18, task-us7sh)

**Not safe to enable yet. It becomes safe once the four items below are done, in this order.** The code fix exists, but the live console still runs the old build. Today vps01 can still read the console with no token (`/v1/devices` → 200). Because the console runs `--pane-pair` with no `--pair-approvers`, vps01 can also approve a QR claim.

What landed:
- Branch `fm/sidecar-tagged-trust-20261019`, commits e50fa09 and 2ffd308. `make check` passes.
- A tagged node never gets tailnet trust (reads) and never approves a pairing. Whois reports it with `Tags` or with the `tagged-devices` owner.
- A node named by the new `--tailnet-distrust <StableID,...>` flag is refused the same way.
- The rule holds even when `--pair-approvers` lists that node, and whatever `Tailscale-User-*` headers the request sends.
- A node once refused is not let back in when whois becomes unavailable. Whois lookups for one address are merged into one, so a flood cannot use up the lookup slots.
- Token, cookie and pane sessions are unchanged. People's devices keep tokenless access.

Evidence: the new build ran on a scratch server at `100.74.138.74:18795` with the live flags. The live console was not touched.

| Request | Result |
|---|---|
| MacBook (a person's node) `GET /v1/devices`, no credential | 200 |
| vps01 `curl -H 'Host: macbook:18795' http://100.74.138.74:18795/v1/devices` | **401** |
| same, with a forged `Tailscale-User-Login: trillium@github` | **401** |
| vps01 `GET /` (html) | 200, the stranger's "Pair this pane" page, not the console |
| vps01 `POST /v1/pane-claims/<code>/approve` on a freshly minted claim | **401** "node vps01.hippo-tilapia.ts.net.: the peer is a tagged node, not a person's device"; the claim stays pending |

Left to do before enable (needs the captain or main OK, since it changes live auth):
1. **DNS:** create `A sidecar.trilliumsmith.com 198.12.123.41` in Vercel DNS (section 2).
2. **Deploy the new build** to the console LaunchAgent copy (`docs/launchd.md`). Agents never run `install`.
3. **Add `--pair-approvers n2nprByHbH11CNTRL,<laptop StableID>`** (the phone, plus the laptop if it should approve) to the console flags in the same deploy. A tagged node is refused even without the list; the list also refuses every other node owned by a person.
4. **Re-test from vps01:** `ssh vps01 "curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -H 'Host: macbook:8791' http://100.74.138.74:8791/v1/devices"` must print **401**. Also check the approve refusal against a freshly minted claim.

Then run section 5 from step 3 onward. The Tailscale ACL (option (a), section 3.4) is still recommended as a second layer, but it no longer blocks enable.

Update (steer-530/532): items 2–4 are **done**. The console runs 72884eb with `--pair-approvers n2nprByHbH11CNTRL,nPK26ob6bX11CNTRL --tailnet-distrust nmwXNTBg7u11CNTRL`.
- vps01 got `/v1/devices` → 401 on 5 consecutive checks, 10s apart. Approve → 401 (tagged node).
- The fallback limit described earlier fired on the first deploy: at load ~410, vps01 got a 200. Commit 72884eb closed it: a peer this process never confirmed now needs its token.
- Evidence: `data/sidecar-tagged-trust-20261019/deploy-evidence-*.md`.
- Only DNS (item 1) and the captain's enable-go remain.

Phone URL (task-us7sh part 3):
- A phone on the tailnet opens **`http://macbook:8791`** and is signed in with no token. Checked from the MacBook on the live console: `:8791/v1/devices` → 200.
- The `https://macbook.hippo-tilapia.ts.net:8792` twin reaches Sidecar from loopback, so it never gets tailnet trust. It shows the QR "Pair this pane" page (`:8792/v1/devices` → 401). That page is what the captain's phone saw.
- Use the twin only for PWA install and Push. Sidecar's README now says this.

## 0.1 Bottom line (original plan)

1. **Hostname:** `sidecar.trilliumsmith.com`, served by the existing vps01 Caddy (v2.11.4). TLS comes from Caddy's automatic Let's Encrypt.
2. **Upstream:** the MacBook's tailnet-only https twin, `https://100.74.138.74:8792` (`tailscale serve` → `127.0.0.1:8791`). Do **not** use the direct tailnet listener `100.74.138.74:8791`.
3. **Auth in front:** none at the edge. Sidecar's own `--require-auth` gate plus QR pairing is the auth, as the captain specified on task-k2354. The edge 404s the approval and operator-only routes.
4. **Vhost file:** `sidecar.trilliumsmith.com.caddy`, next to this report. Syntax was validated offline, and its route matrix was tested on a throwaway loopback Caddy (section 4).
5. **Blockers before enable (captain):**
   - **DNS.** The `*.trilliumsmith.com` wildcard points at Vercel. An explicit A record `sidecar` → `198.12.123.41` is needed in Vercel DNS.
   - **vps01 trust path (pre-existing exposure, found in this inspection).** vps01 can already read the live console with **no credential** (`/v1/devices` → 200 from vps01, section 3.4). Close this before vps01 becomes internet-facing for Sidecar.
6. **Funnel :10000 does not exist today.** `tailscale serve status` has no :10000 entry; AllowFunnel covers only 443 (bridge) and 8443. There is nothing to turn off. Leave 443/8443 alone.
7. **Root on vps01 is no longer blocked.** `ssh vps01 id` → `uid=0(root)`, so task-cipkx does not block the apply. That bead is still open.

## 1. What becomes publicly reachable

The internet reaches `https://sidecar.trilliumsmith.com` (443 on vps01, plus :80 for the ACME/HTTPS redirect). Nothing else is opened: MacBook ports 8791/8792 stay tailnet-only.

| Surface | Public, no credential | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /healthz` | yes | liveness only |
| PWA install: `/manifest.webmanifest`, `/sw.js`, `/icons/*` | yes | static, carries no token (`docs/pwa.md`) |
| Pairing pane side: `POST /v1/pane-claims`, `GET/DELETE /v1/pane-claims/{id}`, `POST /v1/pane-claims/{id}/claim`, the QR page at `/` | yes, only when the console runs `--pane-pair` | rate limited 2/s per peer and 10/s total, at most 16 live claims (`docs/pairing.md`) |
| Refusal pages (401 with a "what to do" page) | yes | script-free and credential-free (`internal/server/guide.go`) |
| Everything else under `/v1/*`, `/ui/*`, `/apps/*` | no: 401 | needs an admin/device token, the `sidecar_access` cookie, or a QR `sidecar_pane` cookie |
| `/pair`, `/pair/*`, `POST /v1/pane-claims/{code}/approve`, `GET /v1/pane-claims` | **404 at the edge** | approval stays on the tailnet twin |
| `/v1/doctor`, `/v1/audit`, `/v1/notify`, `/v1/commands`, `/v1/show`, `/v1/join-tokens*`, `PUT/DELETE /v1/apps/*` | **404 at the edge** | operator-only; the CLI and MCP keep using loopback or the tailnet |

Admin sign-in with `?token=` still works from the internet; that is Sidecar's gate. The edge denylist limits what a leaked admin token can do from outside the tailnet. Caddy's log drops the `token` query value.

## 2. Hostname and TLS

1. Name: `sidecar.trilliumsmith.com`. It matches the `<service>.trilliumsmith.com` pattern of the bridge plan (task-pt5ji: `bridge.trilliumsmith.com`).
2. DNS: `trilliumsmith.com` NS is Vercel (`ns1/ns2.vercel-dns.com`). A wildcard `*.trilliumsmith.com` resolves to Vercel (216.198.79.1/65, 64.29.17.1), so `sidecar.trilliumsmith.com` points at Vercel **today**. An explicit `A sidecar 198.12.123.41` record beats the wildcard. Create it **before** the Caddy reload, or the ACME HTTP/TLS-ALPN challenge lands on Vercel and fails (then retries with backoff).
3. TLS: Caddy's automatic HTTPS issues a Let's Encrypt certificate (as for `vps01.trilliumsmith.com`). It needs no extra config. HSTS is set without `includeSubDomains`, so other `*.trilliumsmith.com` hosts are unaffected.
4. Leg two (vps01 → MacBook) is https to the tailnet twin. Caddy verifies the MacBook's `macbook.hippo-tilapia.ts.net` certificate with `tls_server_name`. tailscaled picks the serve handler by **SNI** (`ipn/ipnlocal/serve.go:824-835`, v1.104.1), so the SNI must be the ts.net name while the Host header stays public.

1. **Decide which of two things you mean.**
   - **Reach the Sidecar console from the internet** (your phone away from the tailnet): this is already planned. The plan is `sidecar.trilliumsmith.com` through vps01's Caddy, with Sidecar's own token and QR pairing as the gate. It is written but not enabled. Still open: one DNS A record in Vercel, a deploy of the current build, and your go to enable. Source: `macbook-ops/data/sidecar-vps01-proxy-plan-20261019/report.md`.

2. **For a contact form, build a small separate service on vps01.** Give it one POST route that accepts a short message, with a captcha (Cloudflare Turnstile or similar), rate limits per IP, and a size cap. It writes to an intake store, such as the `inbox` beads, and never touches Sidecar's panes or console. The console stays tailnet-only.
3. **Expect spam.** Any public write gets bots within hours. The captcha and rate limit are not optional.
4. **Your call:** a public endpoint is outward-facing, so I won't build or deploy one without your explicit go. Tell me which of the two you want, and I'll write it up.
